data.title: Spotify
data.legal_notes: BGB § 309 Nr. 9 lit. b applies: contracts tacitly renewed roll monthly with maximum 1-month notice. BGB § 312k cancellation button compliant.

data.title: Apple
data.legal_notes: Statutory 24m defect liability (BGB § 438 Abs. 1 Nr. 3). 12m reversed burden of proof (BGB § 477 Abs. 1). Apple 1-Year Limited Manufacturer Guarantee (BGB § 443) does not limit statutory seller claims.

data.title: MediaMarkt
data.legal_notes: Seller is liable for 24 months (BGB § 437). § 286 ZPO allows alternative proof of purchase (bank statement) if receipt is lost. Retailer cannot demand manufacturer RMA referral.

data.title: Amazon Prime
data.legal_notes: BGB § 309 Nr. 9 rolling 1-month cancellation. Prime student subscriptions refund pro-rata if unused benefits remain.

data.title: Netflix
data.legal_notes: Monthly rolling billing. Compliant with BGB § 312k 2-step cancellation button. Termination takes effect at end of current billing period.

data.title: Adobe Creative Cloud
data.legal_notes: Student discount annual plans paid monthly. Under German law (BGB § 309 Nr. 9), post-first-year renewal must allow monthly cancellation without early termination penalty fees.

data.title: Microsoft 365
data.legal_notes: Office 365 single/family. Complies with BGB § 312k. Surface hardware purchases carry statutory 24-month seller defect liability under BGB § 438.

data.title: Deutsche Bahn (Deutschlandticket)
data.legal_notes: Deutschlandticket subscription must be cancelled by the 10th of each month for the subsequent month per tariff terms, compliant with BGB § 309 Nr. 9.

data.title: GitHub Pro / Copilot
data.legal_notes: Developer tools qualify as 100% digital tax write-offs under BMF 22.02.2022 decree without GWG ceiling.

data.title: JetBrains
data.legal_notes: Free student licenses renew annually with university email. Commercial renewals subject to monthly/annual terms under BGB § 309.

data.title: YouTube Premium
data.legal_notes: Monthly subscription cancellable at any time before next billing date. BGB § 312k 2-step button compliant.

data.title: Saturn
data.legal_notes: Identical statutory terms to MediaMarkt. BGB § 439 gives buyer remedy choice between repair or replacement.

data.title: Otto
data.legal_notes: Statutory 24m Gewährleistung under BGB § 438. Otto also offers 30-day extended voluntary return policy for distance sales.

data.title: Mindfactory
data.legal_notes: PC hardware components. BGB § 477 12-month reversed burden of proof protects against retailer claims that pins or sockets were user-damaged.

data.title: Notion Plus
data.legal_notes: Productivity SaaS tool qualifying as 100% tax-deductible digital workspace asset under BMF 22.02.2022.

data.title: Gymshark
data.legal_notes: Textile and fitness gear. Statutory 24-month defect liability under BGB §§ 434, 438 applies to zipper and seam defects.

data.title: McFIT / RSG Group
data.legal_notes: Fitness studio contracts. Following BGB § 309 Nr. 9 lit. b reform, post-initial-term renewals are strictly limited to monthly rolling termination.

data.title: Urban Sports Club
data.legal_notes: Flexible sports membership. BGB § 312k 2-step button compliant with 1-month cancellation notice.

data.title: Disney+
data.legal_notes: Streaming subscription. BGB § 312k compliant. Rolling monthly renewal after initial billing.

data.title: Vodafone
data.legal_notes: Telecommunication contracts (TKG § 56 & BGB § 309 Nr. 9). After 24-month minimum term, contracts roll indefinitely with a maximum 1-month notice period.

data.title: Online cancellation button
data.summary: BGB § 312k covers paid continuing consumer contracts that a business lets consumers conclude on its website, subject to statutory exceptions.

takeaways.text: The covered website must provide an easy-to-find cancellation button and a confirmation step. The consumer should receive an electronic confirmation.
If the required button and confirmation page are not provided, a consumer can generally cancel the covered contract at any time without notice. This is not a universal rule for every contract.

data.title: Renewal terms for recurring services
data.summary: BGB § 309 No. 9 limits certain standard contract terms for regular supplies of goods and services.

takeaways.text: For covered terms, an initial binding term may not exceed two years. After that, a tacit renewal must be indefinite and cancellable at any time with no more than one month’s notice.
The rule has exceptions, including insurance and certain contracts for goods sold together. Check the contract and the type of service.
For contracts formed before 1 March 2022, transitional rules may affect which version applies. Check EGBGB Article 229 § 60.

data.title: Withdrawal is different from cancellation
data.summary: A withdrawal right can apply to qualifying distance or off-premises contracts. It is separate from ending an ongoing subscription.

takeaways.text: A 14-day period generally applies to qualifying contracts, but statutory exceptions apply and the starting point depends on the contract and what was bought.
Do not treat withdrawal as a general right to cancel any subscription at any time.

data.title: Statutory rights for faulty goods
data.summary: For a consumer purchase from a trader, statutory defect rights are generally asserted against the seller. They are separate from a manufacturer’s commercial guarantee.

takeaways.text: Repair or replacement is generally the first remedy. Price reduction or ending the contract may be available under statutory conditions.
For ordinary goods, defect claims are generally subject to a two-year limitation period from delivery. Exceptions and special rules apply.
If a defect appears within the first year, it is generally presumed to have existed at delivery unless an exception applies. This affects proof; it does not guarantee an automatic refund.

data.title: Commercial guarantees
data.summary: A commercial guarantee is a voluntary promise by its named guarantor, with its own coverage and claim procedure.

takeaways.text: A guarantee adds to statutory seller rights; it does not replace or reduce them.
Check who gave the guarantee, which product it covers, how long it lasts and how to make a claim.

data.title: EU rules for goods conformity
data.summary: Directive (EU) 2019/771 sets a shared EU framework for consumer sales of goods. National law implements the rules, so local details can differ.

takeaways.text: The Directive generally makes the seller liable for a lack of conformity that appears within two years of delivery.
It provides a one-year presumption about when a defect existed, while allowing Member States to provide a longer period. Use the national law that applies to the purchase.

data.title: Which law applies across borders?
data.summary: Rome I can preserve a consumer’s mandatory home-country protections when a trader directs activity to the country where the consumer habitually lives.

takeaways.text: This protection depends on the facts and the contract being within the rule’s scope. A chosen-law clause does not automatically settle the question.
Check the country, seller, purchase channel and contract before relying on a national rule.

data.title: Statutory defect rights
data.label: Gewährleistung · Germany
data.description: Ordinary consumer-goods defect claims are generally subject to a two-year limitation period from delivery. A defect appearing within the first year is generally presumed to have existed at delivery, subject to exceptions. That presumption concerns proof, not an automatic refund.

data.title: Renewal and cancellation
data.label: BGB §§ 309 and 312k · Germany
data.description: Some recurring-service renewal terms are limited to an indefinite renewal with no more than one month’s notice after the initial term. Covered online contracts may also require a cancellation button. Contract type and statutory exceptions matter.

data.title: Receipt fingerprint integrity
data.label: On-device record · SHA-256
data.description: The app stores a SHA-256 digest with the encrypted receipt and checks the decrypted bytes against it. Comparing a newly computed digest with the stored digest can detect changes to the saved bytes; it does not prove who issued the receipt, when it was created, or that the starting image was truthful.

data.title: Subscriptions
data.description: Practice the difference between ending a contract and withdrawing from it.

data.title: Warranties & faulty goods
data.description: Learn who to contact and what a time limit or guarantee actually means.

data.prompt: You want to stop an ongoing streaming plan. What is cancellation (Kündigung)?

options.label: Ending an ongoing contract for the future
Undoing any purchase within 14 days, without exceptions
Asking the bank to reverse every payment
Deleting the app from your phone

data.explanation: Cancellation ends an ongoing contract. Withdrawal can apply to a qualifying new distance contract, but it has separate conditions and exceptions.

data.prompt: A paid continuing contract was offered and concluded on a trader’s website. If the required cancellation flow is missing, what may § 312k allow?

options.label: A full refund of every past payment
Cancellation of the covered contract at any time without notice
Cancellation only at the end of the original term
No change; online cancellation rules never apply

data.explanation: For contracts within § 312k and outside its exceptions, missing required buttons and confirmation page can let a consumer cancel without a notice period.

data.prompt: For a covered recurring service, what can a standard renewal clause generally provide after the initial term?

options.label: An indefinite renewal cancellable at any time with no more than one month’s notice
A new two-year fixed term in every case
A three-month cancellation period in every case
No cancellation rights at all

data.explanation: BGB § 309 No. 9 limits certain standard terms for recurring supplies of goods and services. Exceptions and the contract type matter.

data.prompt: Before starting a free trial, which details are useful to record?

options.label: Trial end date, paid price, renewal timing and how to cancel
Only the app icon colour
The company’s office opening hours
Nothing; every trial ends automatically

data.explanation: Save the trial end date, price after trial, renewal timing and cancellation route. A covered online contract may also have a § 312k cancellation button; contract terms still matter.

data.prompt: A defect appears in a product within one year of delivery. What does the German presumption generally do?

options.label: Guarantee an immediate refund
Presume the defect existed at delivery, subject to exceptions
Prove that the manufacturer caused the defect
Extend every commercial guarantee to two years

data.explanation: The presumption concerns when the defect existed. It does not decide the remedy or guarantee a refund.

data.prompt: For statutory defect rights on a consumer purchase from a trader, who is normally responsible?

options.label: The seller under the purchase contract
Only the manufacturer
The delivery company in every case
The payment provider

data.explanation: Statutory defect rights are generally asserted against the seller. A separate commercial guarantee may name a different guarantor.

data.prompt: A manufacturer’s voluntary commercial guarantee has expired. What does that tell you about statutory rights against the seller?

options.label: They always expire at the same time
They may still exist under separate statutory rules
The seller must provide a new manufacturer guarantee
The purchase is automatically refunded

data.explanation: A commercial guarantee is separate from statutory seller rights. Check the purchase date, defect, seller and applicable limitation rules.

data.prompt: Which records are useful to keep after buying a product?

options.label: Receipt or order confirmation, plus product and guarantee details
Only the delivery box
Only a screenshot of the shop homepage
No records; the seller always has everything

data.explanation: Keep proof of purchase and the product or guarantee terms so you can identify the seller, item and any separate guarantor when you make a claim.
